Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give my statement without my name on it, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine for this test file. Can you tell me where the accident happened?
A: It was on a multi-lane road in Pasadena, Texas, near a shopping center. I was in the rihgt lane heading toward the
interchange.
Q: What time of day was it, and what were the road conditions?
A: Mid-afternoon. It was dry, and traffic was moving steadily but not stopped.
Q: Walk me through what you were doing when the contact happened.
A: I was signaling to move into the left lane bceause I needed to get over for my exit. I checked my mirror, saw the
lane looked clear, and started to merge. Then the other car came up beside me and clipped the side of my vehicle.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you began to change lanes?
A: Not clearly. I glanced at my mirror and didn't see anything close enough to worry about.
Q: How fast were you each going?
A: I'd estimate around the speed limit, maybe a little under. I'm not certain about the other driver's speed.
Q: Did the other driver stop, and did you exchange information?
A: Yes, they pulled over just ahead. We exchanged insurance and contact details, and I took a few photos of the
damage.
Q: Did you feel any injury at the scene?
A: My neck felt stiff rgiht away, and by that evening I had pain across the back and sides of my neck. I went to a clinic
the next day and was told I had a neck strain.
Q: Are you currently receiving treatment?
A: Yes, I'm going to physical therapy a few times a week, and my doctor has me on a light work restriction for now.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm trying to cooperate fully and I'll send over any records you need.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
